market.summary: The KLCI edged up 0.03% to 1,630.87 after touching 1,640.78 early, so Thursday's 1,630 low held but the bounce faded. Breadth was mildly positive (585 gainers vs 541 losers) and chip stocks led, but banks and plantations stayed weak and the index is down 2.6% this week. It remains below its 10-month average (1,695.0) with the 5-month average below the 10-month, so the market check fails: no buying. Rakuten Trade stays cautious because of high bond yields and oil prices. A close back above about 1,695 is needed before the rule turns.

catalysts.title: CRESS green-power deals for data centres — more to follow
catalysts.when: First deal signed 28 Sep; more expected over Q4 2026
catalysts.theme: Solar / green power for data centres
catalysts.detail: A JV of SD Guthrie (33.5%), Gamuda (33%) and Gentari (33.5%) signed a 21-year CRESS term sheet with a US tech company for at least 680MW of solar plus 4-hour battery storage in Perak, worth over RM10bn of revenue, running from 2029. It confirms the 30% green-power rule is turning into real contracts. HLIB expects Solarvest and Samaiden to sign their first CRESS projects within three months. RHB (22 Sep) says several developers are in the final stages of signing and expects Solarvest to win 300–500MW by end-2026; projects must be commissioned by end-2028. The installers have already run and are consolidating; the supply chain (cables, switchgear, substations) has not moved as much.
